scope: Live FBI CDE / Documents & Downloads / public-data surface survey plus BJS NIBRS estimate materials and the user-identified Princeton and ICPSR explanatory references, with practical implications for V2 source lanes.

sources_surveyed.role: Official methodology guardrail for differences between publication tables and CDE/open-data style surfaces.
Official catalog of current downloadable FBI surfaces: CIUS annual reports, state NIBRS data, master files, SRS estimated crimes, participation, NIBRS estimation tables.
Official machine-readable agency roster and participation metadata.
Official explanation of the post-2021 NIBRS estimate family.
Official machine-readable BJS estimate surface, including current and archive endpoints.
Official publication rendering of the current BJS estimate series.
Official secondary analytic tool using NIBRS with its own coverage/definition rules.
Secondary explanatory map of UCR/NIBRS families and commonly used derivative files.
Secondary archival taxonomy of UCR components and legacy series structure.

top_findings.finding: The official FBI/BJS ecosystem is not a single interchangeable crime surface. V2 has to classify each input lane before selecting a source.
top_findings.practical_implication: Do not talk about 'using CDE' as if that were one dataset. Use publication tables, raw/open-data/master, roster/participation metadata, and BJS estimate surfaces only for their intended lane.

top_findings.finding: The live FBI CDE methodology page explicitly states that annual publication tables can differ from CDE/explorer/open-data style surfaces because publication tables apply internal quality-review criteria, while master/open-data style releases keep all reported data in file.
top_findings.practical_implication: V2 should treat publication-style annual controls and raw reported-universe engineering as separate official lanes. Differences between them are not automatically data corruption.

top_findings.finding: CDE Explorer and the Data Discovery Tool are dynamic, timestamped query surfaces. They are useful for lookups and anomaly checks, but they are not the clean annual-control surface.
top_findings.practical_implication: Use Explorer/DDT for monitoring and reconciliation, then source annual controls from CIUS annual bundles or estimate APIs/downloads.

top_findings.finding: The official roster API and participation downloads are crucial, but they are metadata/coverage surfaces rather than crime-total surfaces.
top_findings.practical_implication: Use roster for ORI validation and effective-year NIBRS auditing; use participation for state-year coverage context; do not treat either as the crime input.

top_findings.finding: BJS/FBI NIBRS estimates for 2021+ are a separate estimate family from the older SRS-derived FBI estimated-crime series.
top_findings.practical_implication: V2 must decide deliberately whether a lane wants reported counts, legacy FBI estimated counts, or BJS/FBI NIBRS estimates. These are not interchangeable controls.

top_findings.finding: Princeton and ICPSR are useful because they map the ecosystem and archival component structure clearly, but they should not outrank the official FBI/BJS surfaces when selecting numeric inputs.
top_findings.practical_implication: Use them to understand where files come from and what families exist; then go back to the official surface for actual ingestion.

fbi_publication_style_annual_controls.reason: This keeps the lane inside the FBI publication-table methodology.

raw_incident_or_master_engineering.reason: This lane wants the full reported universe or incident-level detail, not publication-screened totals or estimate outputs.

agency_roster_and_transition_audit.reason: Roster/participation surfaces answer metadata and coverage questions, not annual crime totals.

official_nibrs_estimate_benchmarks.reason: The estimate lane has its own methodology, revision behavior, and reliability/suppression logic.

official_dynamic_monitoring_and_reconcil.reason: These tools are best for triage and contextual comparisons, not for canonical annual inputs.

methodology_difference_hotspots.why_it_happens: Publication tables apply internal quality-review and completeness rules; master/open-data style files keep all reported data in file.
methodology_difference_hotspots.what_to_do_in_v2: Never label these differences as errors until the lane has been matched.

methodology_difference_hotspots.why_it_happens: Explorer is dynamic, timestamped, and can summarize violent/property data differently while annual publications are static bundles.
methodology_difference_hotspots.what_to_do_in_v2: Use Explorer to investigate, not to replace the annual control table.

methodology_difference_hotspots.why_it_happens: Raw is_nibrs is current status; year-specific policy depends on whether nibrs_start_date is effective in the target year.
methodology_difference_hotspots.what_to_do_in_v2: Compute an effective-year flag before source-selection or mismatch scoring.

methodology_difference_hotspots.why_it_happens: The older series is SRS-derived; the newer series is a NIBRS-based estimate system using weighting/imputation with revision and suppression logic.
methodology_difference_hotspots.what_to_do_in_v2: Keep them separate unless an explicit bridge rule is documented.

methodology_difference_hotspots.why_it_happens: LEARCAT uses full-reporter-state coverage rules and some offense definitions that differ from CDE.
methodology_difference_hotspots.what_to_do_in_v2: Treat LEARCAT as secondary analytic context only.

doctrine_candidates_for_tracker.statement: Before using any FBI/BJS source, classify the lane as publication table, raw/open-data/master, roster/participation metadata, dynamic monitoring, or BJS NIBRS estimate. Source choice happens after lane classification, not before.
Treat FBI publication tables and CDE/master/open-data surfaces as separate official methodologies. Differences between them are expected unless the question has been converted into the same lane.
Use CDE Explorer and the Data Discovery Tool for monitoring, lookups, and reconciliation. Use downloadable annual bundles or documented estimate APIs for canonical V2 inputs.
Use the public CDE roster for ORI metadata and effective-year NIBRS auditing; use participation data for state-year coverage context. Neither should be treated as the crime-total input.
Keep legacy FBI SRS estimated-crime series and BJS/FBI NIBRS estimate series separate unless a bridge rule is explicitly documented.
Use Princeton and ICPSR to understand the UCR/NIBRS ecosystem and archival component structure, but do not let them outrank the official FBI/BJS source surface when selecting inputs.

unresolved_or_follow_up_items.issue: The live downloads page requires selection interaction to expose exact file members for each bundle.
unresolved_or_follow_up_items.practical_next_step: If needed later, capture bundle member lists or filenames for the specific CIUS/NIBRS/master datasets V2 actually ingests.

unresolved_or_follow_up_items.issue: The Crime Data API documentation should be inventoried endpoint-by-endpoint only when V2 is ready to replace a concrete lane with an API pull.
unresolved_or_follow_up_items.practical_next_step: Avoid treating 'the API' as one source; map endpoints to the same lane taxonomy used in this packet.
